sentences.text: The scientific name of this extinct animal is Dunstanetta johnstoneorum.
It is an extinct species of duck from the Miocene of New Zealand.
The species was described based on a fossil distal left humerus found at the Saint Bathans Fauna site on Home Hills Station.
The fossil material was found in the lower Bannockburn Formation of the Manuherikia Group in the Manuherikia River valley of the Central Otago region on New Zealand's South Island.
The genus name Dunstanetta refers to the Dunstan Range, which overlooks the fossil site.
The specific epithet johnstoneorum honors Ann and Euan Johnstone of Home Hills Station.
The genus Dunstanetta is classified within the family Anatidae.
The genus Dunstanetta belongs to the subfamily Oxyurinae.
Fossils of Dunstanetta date to the Early Miocene epoch.
The time range for Dunstanetta is from the Burdigalian to the Langhian, between 18.7 and 15.9 million years ago.
